front.title: Scientific Constitutional Constraints for Evidence-Governed Agentic Internet Operations

abstract.t: This document proposes SCC-1, an experimental profile for preserving evidentiary, authorization, and effect-enforcement boundaries in agent-mediated Internet operations. The term constitutional describes a locally adopted set of durable technical constraints; it does not refer to any national constitution, create law, or determine legal validity. SCC-1 separates authentication, attestation, evidence appraisal, policy authority, delegated scope, action approval, sink admission, execution, and observed outcomes. It specifies fail-closed state transitions, auditable claim promotion, and bounded closure statements for explicitly scoped sinks. This document does not introduce a new credential or OAuth grant. Its claims remain experimental: reported local Python/SQLite and Go/file- state experiments are not independent cross-host verification or production security certification.
